definition: the subjects and content that a school or course teaches
example: A broad curriculum gives pupils the chance to discover talents that exams do not measure.

definition: an outline of the topics to be covered in a particular course
example: The lecturer handed out a syllabus on the first day and explained how each unit would be assessed.

definition: the methods and principles of teaching
example: Effective pedagogy depends less on technology than on how well a teacher understands each learner.

definition: money paid for being taught at a school or university
example: Rising tuition fees have discouraged many able students from low-income families from applying.

definition: money awarded to a student to pay for their studies because of high achievement
example: She won a full scholarship to study engineering at a leading university abroad.

definition: a sum of money given to a student who needs financial help
example: A small bursary covered her textbooks and travel costs during the first year.

definition: the ability to understand and work with numbers
example: Employers frequently complain that school leavers lack basic numeracy.

definition: relating to the skills and training needed for a particular job
example: Vocational courses give teenagers practical skills that are in demand in the local economy.

definition: required by law or by a rule
example: Education is compulsory until the age of sixteen in most countries.

definition: relating to education at university or college level, after school
example: Participation in tertiary education has doubled across the region in a generation.

definition: a student who is studying for a first degree at university
example: Most undergraduates in the faculty live on campus during their first year.

definition: relating to study done after a first university degree
example: Postgraduate study can improve career prospects but often means taking on further debt.

definition: a long piece of written work on a specific topic, done for a university degree
example: Her dissertation examined how small rural schools cope with limited funding.

definition: copying another person's work or ideas and presenting them as your own
example: Universities use special software to detect plagiarism in student essays.

definition: the process of judging how well someone has learned or performed
example: Continuous assessment reduces the pressure that a single final exam places on students.

definition: work done by students during a course that counts towards their final grade
example: Most of my grade comes from coursework rather than from the final exam.

definition: learning by repeating information until it is memorised, without necessarily understanding it
example: Rote learning may help pupils pass tests but rarely develops deeper understanding.

definition: the ability to analyse information objectively and judge it carefully
example: Schools should teach critical thinking so that young people can question what they read online.

definition: the level of success a student reaches in their studies
example: Educational attainment is strongly linked to the income of a child's parents.

definition: the act of staying away from school without permission
example: Truancy often signals deeper problems at home or bullying at school.

definition: to leave a course or school before finishing it
example: A significant number of students drop out in the first year because they cannot afford to continue.

definition: a teacher who gives individual or small-group lessons
example: My personal tutor reviewed my draft and suggested several ways to improve the argument.

definition: an experienced person who gives advice and support to a less experienced one
example: A good mentor can help new graduates understand how a profession really works.

definition: a person who teaches at a university or college
example: The lecturer encouraged students to challenge her interpretation during the discussion.

definition: a department or group of related subjects within a university
example: She applied to the faculty of medicine, which has the highest entry requirements in the country.

definition: to officially register as a student on a course
example: More than two hundred adults enrolled in the evening literacy classes this term.

definition: the continuing education of people throughout their adult lives
example: Rapid changes in the job market make lifelong learning a necessity rather than a luxury.

definition: education in which students study at home rather than attending classes in person
example: Distance learning allows people who live far from a campus to gain a degree.

definition: relating to activities done outside of normal lessons
example: Extracurricular activities such as debating and music help pupils build confidence.

definition: the influence of people of the same age to behave in a certain way
example: Teenagers are particularly susceptible to peer pressure when choosing what to study.

definition: the practice of making people obey rules, or the self-control this produces
example: Strict discipline can create a calm classroom, but it should not replace encouragement.

definition: the repeated use of power to hurt or frighten weaker people
example: Schools need clear policies to tackle bullying, including the online forms that happen outside lessons.

definition: having exceptional natural ability or talent
example: Gifted pupils may become bored if lessons are not challenging enough.

definition: aiming to include all people and treat them fairly
example: An inclusive classroom allows children with disabilities to learn alongside their peers.

definition: containing pupils of different levels of academic skill
example: Teaching a mixed-ability class requires careful planning so that no pupil is left behind.

definition: admitting only students who pass a test or meet high standards
example: Critics argue that selective schools widen the gap between rich and poor.

definition: a school funded by the government and free to attend
example: Pupils from state schools now make up the majority of the university intake.

definition: a school where pupils live during the term
example: Many parents regard a boarding school as a way to give children independence early.

definition: official recognition that a course or institution meets required standards
example: The college lost its accreditation after inspectors found serious weaknesses in teaching.

definition: to complete a university degree
example: She hopes to graduate with a first-class degree in economics next summer.

definition: the set of skills that make a person attractive to employers
example: Universities increasingly stress employability by arranging work placements for undergraduates.

definition: abilities such as communication that are useful in many different jobs
example: Team projects help students acquire transferable skills such as negotiation and time management.

definition: to learn something so well that you can remember it exactly
example: I used to memorise whole chapters before exams, but I forgot almost everything within a week.

definition: the ability to understand something
example: Reading comprehension improves when pupils discuss texts rather than simply read them silently.

definition: relating to mental processes such as thinking, learning and remembering
example: Early play-based learning supports cognitive development in young children.

definition: the ability to produce original ideas
example: Overloaded timetables can stifle creativity by leaving no time for open-ended projects.

definition: the desire or reason that makes someone want to do something
example: Praise from teachers is a powerful source of motivation for young learners.

definition: a strong wish to know or learn something
example: Good teachers spark curiosity by linking lessons to the questions children already ask.

definition: the ability to make your own decisions and act independently
example: Giving students more autonomy over their projects can raise engagement considerably.

definition: to give someone so much help that they do not learn to think for themselves
example: Teachers who spoon-feed their classes may produce students who struggle at university.

definition: involving direct practical experience rather than theory
example: Hands-on experience in a laboratory helps pupils remember scientific ideas more easily.

definition: based on ideas and principles rather than practical application
example: Some graduates complain that their courses were too theoretical to prepare them for work.

definition: a small-group teaching session between students and a tutor
example: In tutorials, students can debate ideas in a way that is impossible in a large lecture hall.

definition: a class in which a small group discusses a topic with a teacher
example: Each seminar begins with a short presentation followed by an open discussion.

definition: designed so that all students take the same test under the same conditions
example: Standardised tests allow fair comparison between schools but may narrow the curriculum.

definition: having very important consequences for the person who takes it
example: High-stakes exams can cause serious anxiety among teenagers.

definition: a steady rise in the marks awarded without a matching rise in student achievement
example: Employers worry that grade inflation has made degree classifications less meaningful.

definition: a published ranking of schools or universities by performance
example: League tables encourage schools to focus narrowly on exam results.

definition: the number of pupils in a single teaching group
example: Smaller class sizes allow teachers to give each child more individual attention.

definition: the time or date by which something must be finished
example: Missing a deadline can lower your final grade by an entire level.

definition: the process of studying again material that has already been learned, before an exam
example: Good revision relies on testing yourself rather than simply rereading notes.

definition: to take an exam again after failing it
example: Students who fail the module must resit the exam during the summer.

definition: former students of a school or university
example: Wealthy alumni often donate large sums to fund new buildings and scholarships.

definition: the land and buildings of a university or college
example: Living on campus makes it easier to take part in clubs and societies.

definition: the act of accepting someone into a school or university
example: Admission to the most competitive courses is based on both grades and interviews.

definition: a year between school and university spent travelling or working
example: Taking a gap year can help young people mature before they start their degree.

definition: study at university or college level after finishing school
example: Expanding higher education has widened opportunities but has also raised questions about quality.

definition: the inability to read and write
example: Illiteracy remains a barrier to employment and political participation in many regions.

definition: considering the whole person rather than only one part
example: A holistic approach to schooling values social and emotional growth as well as exam results.

definition: having a balanced range of skills and interests
example: Schools should aim to produce well-rounded citizens rather than only high exam scorers.

definition: to gradually put an idea or habit into someone's mind
example: Primary teachers play a vital role in instilling a love of reading.

definition: to care for and encourage the growth or development of someone
example: Good schools nurture talent regardless of a child's background.

definition: to encourage something to become more active or develop
example: Interactive lessons can stimulate interest even in subjects that pupils find difficult.

definition: to develop a quality or skill through effort
example: Universities should cultivate independent thinking rather than simply deliver information.
